used.how: unified path keeps the stored [N, K] bfp8 / bfp4 weights; the fork option weights_transposed reads them transposed inside the op instead of uploading W^T (which rounds 48 matrices)
the routing weight keeps travelling as three bf16 pieces in the dispatched row; one selector matmul per chunk (one product per tile-dot) turns them into the op's fp32 routing_weights

the selector matmul is exact by the one-nonzero-per-tile-dot rule; the 2.6 % fp8 differences of the first unit test were traced to this in-tile GEMM rounding, so the exact test uses selection weights (DS41-60)
the in-kernel fp8 q-dq reproduces tt/quant.fp8_qdq's arithmetic (clamp 1e-4, fp32(1/448), ue8m0 from the bits, e4m3 RNE on the integer bits, subnormal step 2^-9)
the h options unpack the Float32 gate / up partials straight into the fp32 DEST (UnpackToDestFp32) instead of through SrcA at TF32 (DS41-58)
the unified call keeps high_precision=True with HiFi4 + fp32 dest (ROW_MAJOR bf16 x)
counts / region offsets passed as the global [1, E] vectors from offset_cumsum
the dispatched buffer is freed only after the op returned (ROW_MAJOR x gives a fresh output)
read the hand-run profile metrics from generated/bringup_adhoc/P.2.json
--no-precompile on every model-sized and fork test run
fork unit tests open the box's full 2x2 FABRIC_2D mesh with require_exact_physical_num_devices

copy_tile of a Float32 CB reads through SrcA (TF32) unless the CB is UnpackToDestFp32 (DS41-58)
